---
title: "Quiz on spatial networks"
filters:
  - naquiz
---

Check how much you remember from this section by answering the questions below.

:::::{.question}
**In a street network, what do nodes and edges usually represent?**

::::{.choices}

:::{.choice .correct-choice}
Nodes represent intersections, and edges represent street segments connecting them.
:::

:::{.choice}
Nodes represent streets, and edges represent the buildings along them.
:::

:::{.choice}
Nodes represent travel costs, and edges represent geographic areas.
:::

:::{.choice}
Nodes represent destinations, and edges represent travel schedules.
:::

::::
:::::

:::::{.question}
**Why might distance along a street network differ from straight-line distance?**

::::{.choices}

:::{.choice}
Street-network distance is always shorter because it follows streets.
:::

:::{.choice .correct-choice}
The route is constrained by the network, so it may not follow the direct path between two places.
:::

:::{.choice}
Straight-line distance accounts for one-way streets, but network distance does not.
:::

:::{.choice}
They are always equal when the network is made from OpenStreetMap.
:::

::::
:::::

:::::{.question}
**What does `network.nearest_pois()` return?**

::::{.choices}

:::{.choice}
The nearest network node to each point of interest.
:::

:::{.choice}
The number of points of interest within the search area.
:::

:::{.choice .correct-choice}
Distances from network nodes to the nearest point(s) of interest, optionally including their IDs.
:::

:::{.choice}
A polygon showing the area around each point of interest.
:::

::::
:::::

:::::{.question}
**What does an isochrone represent?**

::::{.choices}

:::{.choice}
The shortest route connecting every pair of destinations.
:::

:::{.choice .correct-choice}
The area reachable from one or more origins within a specified time or distance.
:::

:::{.choice}
The straight-line distance from an origin to its nearest destination.
:::

:::{.choice}
The number of network nodes in a geographic area.
:::

::::
:::::

:::::{.question}
**What is the effect of using a linear decay when aggregating values across a network?**

::::{.choices}

:::{.choice}
It gives more influence to values farther away.
:::

:::{.choice}
It removes all values outside the network.
:::

:::{.choice .correct-choice}
It gives less influence to values as network distance increases.
:::

:::{.choice}
It converts distances into travel times using transit schedules.
:::

::::
:::::

:::::{.question}
**Why might values be assigned to the nearest existing network node?**

::::{.choices}

:::{.choice}
To ensure every point is exactly on a street intersection.
:::

:::{.choice .correct-choice}
Network analyses use network nodes, so assigning values to nearby nodes links the data to the network.
:::

:::{.choice}
To convert all values into distances.
:::

:::{.choice}
To remove nodes that are not connected to a street.
:::

::::
:::::

:::::{.question}
**What information does GTFS provide for modelling public transport?**

::::{.choices}

:::{.choice}
Street geometries and road speed limits only.
:::

:::{.choice}
Population counts at transit stops.
:::

:::{.choice .correct-choice}
Transit routes, stops, schedules, transfers, and related service information.
:::

:::{.choice}
The shortest walking route between any two places.
:::

::::
:::::


:::::{.question}
**What does a travel-time matrix contain?**

::::{.choices}

:::{.choice .correct-choice}
Travel times between origin and destination pairs.
:::

:::{.choice}
The coordinates of every intersection in the network.
:::

:::{.choice}
The number of transit routes serving each origin.
:::

:::{.choice}
The polygon boundaries of all reachable areas.
:::

::::
:::::

:::::{.question}
**How can travel times be converted into interaction weights?**

::::{.choices}

:::{.choice}
Assign the same weight to every pair of places, regardless of travel time.
:::

:::{.choice}
Use the straight-line distance between place names.
:::

:::{.choice .correct-choice}
Apply a kernel so that shorter travel times receive higher weights and longer times receive lower weights.
:::

:::{.choice}
Replace travel times with the number of transit stops in the dataset.
:::

::::
:::::
